expectedText:
NEED-BASED ATTORNEY'S FEES IN FAMILY LAW PROCEEDINGS — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Jordan Lee · Pat Morgan

DECLARATION IDENTIFYING THE CASE AND THE FEE REQUEST
This request concerns the family law proceeding between Jordan Lee, Petitioner, and Pat Morgan, Respondent, Case No. 26FL00123, filed in the Superior Court of California, County of Sacramento. ☐ Jordan Lee ☐ Pat Morgan requests an order under Family Code §§ 2030–2032 that the other party pay a reasonable amount toward attorney's fees and costs, based on the parties' respective incomes and needs.

FINDINGS THE COURT MUST MAKE WHEN FEES ARE REQUESTED
Family Code § 2030 states that when a request for attorney's fees and costs is made in a proceeding for dissolution, nullity, or legal separation (or a related proceeding after judgment), the court must make findings on whether an award under that section is appropriate, whether there is a disparity between Jordan Lee and Pat Morgan in access to funds to retain counsel, and whether one of them is able to pay for legal representation of both. If those findings show a disparity in access and in ability to pay, the statute directs the court to make an order awarding attorney's fees and costs. The statute also states that a party who lacks the financial ability to hire an attorney may request, without an attorney, that the court order the other party — if that other party has the financial ability — to pay a reasonable amount so the unrepresented party can retain counsel in a timely manner before the matter proceeds.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "(2) When a request for attorney’s fees and costs is made, the court shall make findings on whether an award of attorney’s fees and costs under this section is appropriate, whether there is a disparity in access to funds to retain counsel, and whether one party is able to pay for legal representation of both parties. If the findings demonstrate disparity in access and ability to pay, the court shall make an order awarding attorney’s fees and costs."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 2030(a)(2) (California Legislative Information text), the court's mandatory findings when a fee request is made (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=2030.)
  "A party who lacks the financial ability to hire an attorney may request, as an in pro per litigant, that the court order the other party, if that other party has the financial ability, to pay a reasonable amount to allow the unrepresented party to retain an attorney in a timely manner before proceedings in the matter go forward."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 2030(a)(2) (California Legislative Information text), a self-represented party's request that the other party fund retaining counsel (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=2030.)
  Known gap: This clause covers Family Code § 2030(a)(2) only — the mandatory-findings requirement and the self-represented-litigant request provision, drawn from two passages within that same paragraph. It does not restate § 2030(a)(1)'s underlying statement of the court's duty to ensure access to legal representation and the income-and-needs standard for ordering fees; that provision is already covered by a separate clause elsewhere in this corpus (in the marital settlement agreement document), and is not re-quoted here to avoid duplicating an existing citation. It does not cover the standard for setting the amount of any award (Family Code § 2032) or the procedural mechanism for requesting a fee order during the pendency of the proceeding (Family Code § 2031); both are addressed in separate clauses. The statute does not itself define 'disparity' numerically, and how a court weighs these findings on any particular record is not stated here.

FEES MAY PREDATE THE CASE AND BE MODIFIED AS IT PROCEEDS
Family Code § 2030(b) states that attorney's fees and costs within that section may be awarded for legal services rendered or costs incurred before or after the proceeding commenced. Family Code § 2030(c) states that the court shall augment or modify an original award of attorney's fees and costs as may be reasonably necessary for the prosecution or defense of the proceeding, or any related proceeding, including after any appeal has concluded.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "(b) Attorney’s fees and costs within this section may be awarded for legal services rendered or costs incurred before or after the commencement of the proceeding."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 2030(b) (California Legislative Information text), fees may cover services or costs before or after the proceeding commenced (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=2030.)
  "(c) The court shall augment or modify the original award for attorney’s fees and costs as may be reasonably necessary for the prosecution or defense of the proceeding, or any proceeding related thereto, including after any appeal has been concluded."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 2030(c) (California Legislative Information text), the court's duty to augment or modify an award as the proceeding continues (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=2030.)
  Known gap: This clause covers Family Code § 2030(b) and (c), two adjacent subdivisions of the same statutory section addressed by the mandatory-findings clause above (§ 2030(a)(2)) and, separately elsewhere in this corpus, by a clause covering § 2030(a)(1); none of the three restates another's quoted text. This clause does not state a cap on how many times an award may be augmented, a deadline for seeking augmentation, or the procedural mechanism for requesting an initial or augmented award — the general motion/order-to-show-cause procedure for a pendency-of-proceeding request is addressed in a separate clause covering Family Code § 2031, which by its own terms governs temporary orders during the pendency of the action rather than the post-appeal augmentation authority described here.

REQUESTING A FEE ORDER DURING THE PROCEEDING: MOTION OR ORDER TO SHOW CAUSE
Family Code § 2031(a)(1) states that, except as provided in § 2031(b), during the pendency of a proceeding for dissolution, nullity, or legal separation (or a related proceeding after judgment), an application for a temporary order making, augmenting, or modifying an award of attorney's fees — including a reasonable retainer to hire an attorney — or costs, or both, is made by motion on notice or by an order to show cause. Family Code § 2031(a)(2) states that the court shall rule on such an application within 15 days of the hearing on the motion or order to show cause. Family Code § 2031(b) states that such an order may instead be made without notice, by an oral motion in open court, at the time of the hearing of the cause on the merits, or at any time before entry of a default judgment under Code of Civil Procedure § 585 or § 586, with the court required to rule on a motion made this way within 15 days and before entry of judgment.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "(a) (1) Except as provided in subdivision (b), during the pendency of a proceeding for dissolution of marriage, for nullity of marriage, for legal separation of the parties, or any proceeding subsequent to entry of a related judgment, an application for a temporary order making, augmenting, or modifying an award of attorney’s fees, including a reasonable retainer to hire an attorney, or costs or both shall be made by motion on notice or by an order to show cause."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 2031(a)(1) (California Legislative Information text), a temporary fee order is sought by noticed motion or order to show cause (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=2031.)
  "(2) The court shall rule on an application within 15 days of the hearing on the motion or order to show cause."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 2031(a)(2) (California Legislative Information text), the 15-day ruling deadline for a noticed motion or order to show cause (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=2031.)
  "(b) An order described in subdivision (a) may be made without notice by an oral motion in open court at either of the following times: (1) At the time of the hearing of the cause on the merits. (2) At any time before entry of judgment against a party whose default has been entered pursuant to Section 585 or 586 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The court shall rule on any motion made pursuant to this subdivision within 15 days and prior to the entry of any judgment."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 2031(b) (California Legislative Information text), the without-notice, oral-motion exception and its ruling deadline (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=2031.)
  Known gap: This clause covers Family Code § 2031(a)(1), (a)(2), and (b) — three subdivisions/paragraphs of the same statutory section, independent of the fee-standard sections addressed in the other clauses in this set (§ 2030 and § 2032). It states the statutory pathways and ruling deadlines for a temporary fee order sought during the proceeding; it does not state what Judicial Council form or local court procedure is used in practice (commonly a Request for Order), does not address a request for fees made otherwise than during the pendency of the action (e.g., at judgment or on appeal, addressed by § 2030(c) in a separate clause), and does not address the cross-referenced Code of Civil Procedure default-judgment provisions beyond citing their section numbers.

THE "JUST AND REASONABLE" STANDARD FOR SETTING A FEE AWARD
Family Code § 2032(a) states that the court may make an award of attorney's fees and costs under Family Code § 2030 or § 2031 where the making of the award, and the amount of the award, are just and reasonable under the relative circumstances of the respective parties.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "(a) The court may make an award of attorney’s fees and costs under Section 2030 or 2031 where the making of the award, and the amount of the award, are just and reasonable under the relative circumstances of the respective parties."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 2032(a) (California Legislative Information text), the just-and-reasonable standard for both the award and its amount (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=2032.)
  Known gap: This clause covers Family Code § 2032(a) alone, one subdivision of a section that is independent of, but cross-referenced to, § 2030 and § 2031 (each addressed in separate clauses in this set). It states that the 'just and reasonable' standard governs both whether to award fees and how much to award, but it does not itself list what the 'relative circumstances' are — those factors are stated in § 2032(b), covered in a separate clause. It does not state a formula, percentage, or dollar range for a 'just and reasonable' award, and no case law construing that standard is cited here.

FACTORS IN THE "RELATIVE CIRCUMSTANCES" ANALYSIS
Family Code § 2032(b) states that in determining what is just and reasonable under the relative circumstances, the court considers the need for the award to enable each party, to the extent practical, to have sufficient financial resources to present the party's case adequately, taking into consideration, to the extent relevant, the circumstances of the respective parties described in Family Code § 4320. The statute further states that a requesting party's own resources to pay their own attorney's fees and costs are not themselves a bar to an order that the other party pay part or all of the fees and costs requested, and that financial resources are only one factor for the court to consider in apportioning the overall cost of the litigation equitably between the parties under their relative circumstances.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "(b) In determining what is just and reasonable under the relative circumstances, the court shall take into consideration the need for the award to enable each party, to the extent practical, to have sufficient financial resources to present the party’s case adequately, taking into consideration, to the extent relevant, the circumstances of the respective parties described in Section 4320."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 2032(b) (California Legislative Information text), the relative-circumstances factors, cross-referencing § 4320 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=2032.)
  "The fact that the party requesting an award of attorney’s fees and costs has resources from which the party could pay the party’s own attorney’s fees and costs is not itself a bar to an order that the other party pay part or all of the fees and costs requested. Financial resources are only one factor for the court to consider in determining how to apportion the overall cost of the litigation equitably between the parties under their relative circumstances."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 2032(b) (California Legislative Information text), a requesting party's own resources are not themselves a bar to an award (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=2032.)
  Known gap: This clause covers two passages within a single subdivision, Family Code § 2032(b). It cross-references Family Code § 4320 for the circumstances the court considers 'to the extent relevant,' but does not itself quote § 4320's list of factors — § 4320 is a spousal-support statute, and no independent verification of its text was performed for this clause; a reader relying on this clause alone will not see that list. It does not state how much weight any single factor carries relative to the others, or how a court resolves conflicting factors on a particular record.

RELIEF REQUESTED AND STATUTORY BASIS
The requesting party asks the court to find, based on the income and needs assessments of Jordan Lee and Pat Morgan, whether a disparity exists in access to funds to retain counsel and in the parties' respective abilities to pay for legal representation, and to order an amount of attorney's fees and costs that is just and reasonable under the parties' relative circumstances, payable by ☐ Petitioner ☐ Respondent to ☐ the other party ☐ the other party's attorney, in the amount of $ _________________________ , or such other amount as the court determines, pursuant to Family Code §§ 2030–2032.
